title: Greece vs Spain: Which Mediterranean Country Should You Visit?

categories.summary: The biggest cost variable in Greece is which island you choose. faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain cheaper?
faqs.answer: Greece is generally cheaper, though the gap has narrowed. A mid-range daily budget in Greece runs $80–130/person (Athens and mainland) to $100–180 on Santorini or Mykonos. faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain better for beaches?
faqs.answer: Greece wins on pure beach quality — the Aegean and Ionian islands offer some of Europe's most stunning beaches. faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain better for food?
faqs.answer: Spain is widely considered to have the superior food scene. San Sebastián (Donostia) has the highest density of Michelin stars per capita of any city in the world. faqs.question: Which is better — Greek islands or Spanish islands?
faqs.answer: The Greek islands win for scenic drama, clarity of water, and island-hopping culture. faqs.question: Can you combine Greece and Spain in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it makes a superb 2–3 week European itinerary. The easiest routing: fly into Barcelona, spend 3–4 days, fly to Athens (2.5hr direct, $50–150), spend 2–3 days in Athens, then island-hop 5–7 days, fly home from Athens (or back to a European hub).
